The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I found and fixed.

## Summary

The reduction methods in `pandas/core/arrays/masked.py` (`min/max/sum/prod/mean/var/std`) already accepted an `axis` argument and delegated to `pandas/core/array_algos/masked_reductions.py`, but the axis handling was broken for 2D arrays in several ways. I fixed the two source files (no tests touched):

### `masked_reductions.py`

1. **`_minmax` — `skipna=True` on 2D flattened the array.** The old code did `subset = values[~mask]`, which collapses a 2D array to 1D, so `min/max(axis=1)` raised an `AxisError` and `axis=0` returned a scalar. Added a 2D branch that uses `func(values, axis=axis, where=~mask, initial=<identity>)`, with a new `_minmax_initial` helper that returns the dtype's max (for `min`) or min (for `max`) so masked entries never win. Fully-NA rows/columns collapse to the identity and get masked out by the caller.

2. **`_minmax` and `_reductions` — `skipna=False` on 2D returned a scalar `NA`** whenever *any* value was masked. Added a 2D-axis branch that computes the full result and lets the caller mask only the affected rows/columns (`_mask.any(axis=...)`).

3. **`mean`/`var`/`std` — the `mask.all()` guard returned a scalar `NA` early** even for an axis reduction of a fully-masked 2D array. Made the guard axis-aware (`mask.all() and (axis is None or values.ndim == 1)`) so those cases produce an array of NAs.

### `masked.py`

4. **`_wrap_min_count_reduction_result` ignored `skipna` for `min_count == 0`.** The fast path applied an all-False mask unconditionally, so `sum(axis=0, skipna=False)` returned valid sums for columns that contained NAs. Gated the fast path on `skipna` so `skipna=False` falls through to the normal `_mask.any(axis=...)` masking.

All existing suites pass (`arrays/integer`, `arrays/floating`, `arrays/masked`, `reductions`, `extension/test_masked`, `frame/test_reductions` — 10,800+ tests), and I verified `axis=0/1/None`, `skipna=True/False`, `min_count=1`, `ddof=0`, fully-masked columns/arrays, and `axis=None == raveled` equivalence for Integer, Floating, and Boolean arrays.
